precepts.text: Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering and the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses had commanded. For Israel, not for everybody.
precepts.point: And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement, the margin says reconciliation. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word: Christ died and brought us back to the Father, which is also called adoption. Christianity starts Romans 5 in the middle where it is confusing; start earlier and it is clear.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Romans 5:11 says “by whom we have now received the atonement”, and the margin gives the word reconciliation. Atonement is Christ’s death, which brings us back to the Father. Reconcile in verse 10 and atonement in verse 11 are the same word; that is also called adoption. Atonement is reparation for a wrong or injury: when Christ died on the cross he died for our wrongs. Break the word down in English and it is at-onement: bringing back together again as one. Who did God come to bring together as one? Israel, the two sticks joined together, both kingdoms.

So who was the atonement ever made for? “But Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of the burnt offering, and on the altar of incense, and were appointed for all the work of the place most holy, and to make an atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.” For Israel. Not for everybody.

The theology of the world says atonement is the reconciliation of God and all humankind. But God was never one with all humankind. All nations were never one with Israel, ever. The priesthood of Aaron made atonement for one people, and when Christ made the atonement with his own body, he made it for that same people.

precepts.text: Even in Babylon our captors required of us a song of Zion, proof to the nations of how great our singers were then and are now.
precepts.point: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.”

Even in Babylon our captors required of us a song of Zion. That is proof to the nations of how great our singers were then and are now.

So do not read “these are they whom David set over the service of song in the house of the Lord” as regular men. These were famous men, royalty, chosen singers with musical talent, set apart to minister before the house of the Most High.

precepts.text: It is the prince's part, the Levites, to give the burnt offerings and make reconciliation for the house of Israel.
precepts.point: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“And it shall be the prince’s part to give burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and drink offerings, in the feasts, and in the new moons, and in the sabbaths, in all solemnities of the house of Israel”, and “to make reconciliation for the house of Israel.” It is the prince's part, the Levites, to give the burnt offerings and make reconciliation for Israel.

The singers David set over the service of song were of that tribe. “And they ministered before the dwelling place of the tabernacle of the congregation with singing, until Solomon had built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem: and then they waited on their office according to their order.” The tribe was in right order at this time.

precepts.point: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“Fear the Lord with all thy soul, and reverence his priests.”

The men David set over the service of song were not regular men. They were set apart to minister before the house of the Most High, and they waited on their office according to their order, so they are to be held in reverence.

points: The sons of Levi are named, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, and the line runs through Kohath and Amram to Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: This is a good and honorable lineage, the men who executed the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The priestly line from Aaron is traced through Eleazar, Phinehas, and on down to Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the Most High carried away Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The sons of Levi are set down again by their families: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, with the sons that came from each.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: These are they whom David set over the service of song in the house of the Most High after the ark had rest.
Do not read this as regular men. These were famous men, royalty, chosen singers with musical talent set apart to minister before the house of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: They ministered before the tabernacle of the congregation with singing until Solomon built the house of the Most High, and then they waited on their office according to their order, showing the tribe was in right order at this time.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: These are they that waited with their children, the singers of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman the singer, and his line traced back through Levi to Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: Asaph stood on Heman's right hand and the sons of Merari stood on the left, and their brethren the Levites were appointed to all manner of service of the tabernacle of the house of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: Aaron and his sons offered upon the altar of burnt offering and the altar of incense and did the work of the place most holy, to make an atonement for Israel according to all that Moses commanded.
Without the priests offering the proper sacrifices, the children of Israel could not be reconciled to the Most High after falling into sin, for we did not yet have Christ.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The sons of Aaron are named from Eleazar down to Ahimaaz, the high priestly line.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: These are the dwelling places of the sons of Aaron and the other Levites, the cities and suburbs given them by lot out of the tribes.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 6: The Sons of Levi and the Priesthood

points: The Levites had no land inheritance like the rest of the tribes, so these cities and their suburbs are where they dwelt, given out of Judah, Simeon, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
